title: Archives Live: D-Day
description: Dan Snow presents an archive-led lesson on the experiences of people involved in D-Day. Compare the documents discussed with the academy's Normandy study; a modern educational interpretation is distinct from contemporary evidence.
license: Copyright The National Archives and contributing rights holders; official YouTube embed only. No permission to download or redistribute the film is asserted.
attribution: The National Archives UK, Archives Live: D-Day, broadcast June 2024; presented by Dan Snow.

title: Archives Live: D-Day - Extended Q&A
description: Dan Snow interviews Brigadier Robbie Scott-Bowden in the companion discussion to the archive's D-Day broadcast. Use the interview to consider how later accounts interpret wartime experience.
license: Copyright The National Archives and contributing rights holders; official YouTube embed only. No permission to download or redistribute the film is asserted.
attribution: The National Archives UK, Archives Live: D-Day - Extended Q&A; Dan Snow and Brigadier Robbie Scott-Bowden.

title: Ulysses S. Grant portrait, circa 1865
description: A photographic portrait cataloged around 1865. The institutional record identifies Grant and dates the object; the photograph alone cannot establish his decisions or command ability.
license: Public domain, as stated in the holding institution's item-level rights record.
attribution: Harry S. Truman Library & Museum, accession 60-261; National Archives identifier 348099879.

title: Portrait of Dwight D. Eisenhower, 1960
description: A portrait record dated February 1960 in the Truman Library collection. This later presidential-era representation should not be mistaken for a photograph taken during the Normandy campaign.
license: Public domain, as stated in the holding institution's item-level rights record.
attribution: Harry S. Truman Library & Museum, accession 60-326; National Archives identifier 348100501.

title: Bachelder's map of the Gettysburg battlefield
description: John B. Bachelder's postwar mapping depicts terrain and reconstructed troop positions for the three days of Gettysburg. Compare its detailed survey with the academy's schematic; neither should be treated as an unmediated record of every movement.
license: Library of Congress Geography and Map Division: free to use and reuse unless an item-specific rights advisory states otherwise. The selected record displays no contrary advisory.
attribution: John B. Bachelder; Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division, G3824.G3S5 1863 .B33, item 99447491.

title: Craan's Waterloo battlefield map, 1816
description: Willem Benjamin Craan's early post-battle map, engraved by G. Jacowick, uses colors and symbols to distinguish forces and movement. Study the legend and publication date before comparing it with the simplified Waterloo replay.
license: CC BY 4.0 for the digital copy, according to the institutional catalog. Attribution required; no image modifications are made here.
attribution: W. B. Craan and G. Jacowick, 1816. Fuente: Archivo Cartográfico de Estudios Geográficos del Centro Geográfico del Ejército / Biblioteca Virtual de Defensa. AR.K-T.7-C.1-76.

title: Eisenhower's D-Day Order of the Day
description: Read the June 1944 message and its transcript alongside the Normandy study. Its purpose was to encourage the expeditionary force, so its confident language is evidence of command communication rather than a prediction that victory was certain.
license: Public-domain US federal military document; linked institutional scan and transcript. No third-party images or modern editorial text are reproduced.
attribution: Dwight D. Eisenhower, D-Day statement, June 1944; Eisenhower Pre-Presidential Papers, Dwight D. Eisenhower Library, National Archives and Records Administration.

title: Eisenhower's prepared message in case D-Day failed
description: The library provides Eisenhower's contingency note and a transcript. Written before the invasion, it accepts responsibility for failure. The handwritten month is mistakenly July; the archive identifies the actual date as June 5, 1944.
license: Public-domain US federal military document; linked institutional collection. No third-party images or modern editorial text are reproduced.
attribution: Dwight D. Eisenhower, In Case of Failure message; Pre-Presidential Papers, Principal File, box 168; National Archives identifier 186470.

title: Articles implementing the surrender at Appomattox, 1865
description: The April 10 agreement records arrangements for the surrender of the Army of Northern Virginia following Grant and Lee's meeting. It concerns one army; other Confederate forces surrendered afterward. Use it to distinguish a battlefield outcome from a war's political conclusion.
license: Public-domain nineteenth-century military document; linked institutional scan and transcript. No modern editorial text is reproduced.
attribution: Articles of Agreement, April 10, 1865; Records of the Adjutant General's Office, Record Group 94; National Archives and Records Administration.
